newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Safrica's Denel breaking into Mideast arms market.
newsitem.headline: Safrica's Denel breaking into Mideast arms market.

text.p: South Africa's state-owned arms maker Denel is breaking into the Middle East market and hopes for sales worth up to $600 million in the volatile region in the next few years, its managing director said on Monday.

"We are marketing our products throughout the Middle East and are in the first stage of negotiations," Johan Alberts told Reuters. "I expect we will sell between $500 million and $600 million in the area over the next two to three years."
Alberts was speaking on the sidelines of Abu Dhabi's IDEX international arms show which opened on Sunday.

He said Denel was seeking to sell a number of products including reconnaisance aircraft, howitzer guns, Rooivalk attack helicopters, assault rifles, pistols, mortars, anti-mine devices and machineguns.
In the last four years Denel has sold $400 million worth of weapons in the Middle East, excluding Iran, Iraq and Libya, Alberts said.
It sold howitzer guns to Oman last year. Alberts declined to give the number or value of guns sold to the Gulf Arab state.

South Africa's Armaments Corp of South Africa (Armscor), the state's marketing group, says between 35 and 40 percent of its defence industry exports already go to the Middle East, particularly the Gulf states.

President Nelson Mandela and other officials from South Africa, where the defence industry is emerging from its long apartheid isolation, had in the last two years toured Gulf Arab states and promoted arms sales to the oil-rich region.
Denel, which has sold goods to about 80 countries since its establishment in 1992, is facing stiff competition from U.S., French, British, German and Swiss firms in the Middle East.
"The toughest product to sell is the attack helicopter...We are competing with the American Apache helicopter," Alberts said. "Countries in the Middle East will continue to be growth markets."
He said Denel saw Malaysia and India as key Asian markets.
Mandela had earlier this month said that the sale of the country's Rooivalk helicopters to Malaysia was being considered "sympathetically" but no deal had been made yet.
Denel is on South Africa's privatisation list and is expected to be sold this year.
